claims.claim: Control over working arrangements is an object of workplace bargaining.
Workers who cannot refuse last-minute schedule changes must keep personal time available without compensation for that availability.
Short-notice shift changes can disrupt workers' child care, second jobs, classes, sleep, and transport connections.
Workers affected by short-notice scheduling lack control over the timetable governing their travel and personal arrangements.
Short-notice scheduling systems transfer the costs of uncertainty from firms to workers.
Transferring scheduling uncertainty to workers changes their conduct before any actual shift change occurs.
Workers who know their hours may change unpredictably treat their plans as provisional.
Workers decline invitations because of unpredictable scheduling.
Workers postpone appointments because of unpredictable scheduling.
Unpredictable scheduling makes it harder for workers to seek better employment.
Attending job interviews requires workers to have dependable gaps in their schedules.
Employers using unpredictable schedules obtain practical claims on workers' time outside scheduled work.
Workers are not compensated for keeping that off-hours time available to employers.
Scheduling software gives management increased information, speed, and discretion over schedules.
Workers using scheduling software receive shift changes through time-sensitive digital notifications.
Managerial power to impose short-notice scheduling changes exists independently of scheduling software.
Scheduling software automates a preexisting managerial power over workers' schedules.
Managerial short-notice scheduling was coercive before it was implemented through software.
Some short-notice workplace schedule changes are unavoidable.
Worker illness can necessitate workplace schedule changes.
Equipment failure can necessitate workplace schedule changes.
Unexpected demand can necessitate workplace schedule changes.
Making firms bear a cost for short-notice scheduling will cause them to stop treating scheduling uncertainty as free.
Better calendars or faster schedule notifications can lessen the disruption caused by short-notice scheduling.
Work-schedule predictability is sometimes described as an employment benefit.
Short-notice scheduling pushes the costs of uncertainty downward from management or firms to workers.
Short-notice scheduling increases worker obedience to management.
